title: This 150-Million-Year-Old Bird Had Dinosaur Teeth and a Strange Secret
summary:
A crow-sized fossil found in China is shaking up the story of how birds evolved. The 150-million-year-old creature, named Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis, lived in the Late Jurassic period, about 150 to 148 million years ago, and researchers say it may be the earliest known bird lineage to lose the ability to fly.

That is a surprise. Many people picture early birds steadily becoming better and better flyers. This fossil suggests something messier and more interesting: early birds were already trying out different ways of life, including life on the ground.

The fossil was found in the Zhenghe Fauna of Fujian Province in southeastern China and described in a study in Nature by researchers from the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences and the Fujian Institute of Geological Sciences.

Yuezhuornis mixes bird and dinosaur features in a striking way. It had bird-like pelvic and hindlimb structures, but its jaws held closely spaced, serrated teeth like those of deinonychosaurs, a group of small meat-eating dinosaurs related to birds. Its second toe could bend backward unusually far and carried a curved, sickle-shaped claw, another feature strongly linked to predatory dinosaurs such as dromaeosaurids and troodontids.

To place it on the family tree, scientists compared its anatomy using two methods, maximum parsimony and Bayesian tip-dating. Both put Yuezhuornis firmly within Avialae, the group that includes modern birds and their closest extinct relatives, just beyond Archaeopteryx and as a close relative of Zhengheornis.

Measurements of its limb proportions also pointed to the ground. They closely resembled those of modern ground-dwelling birds, suggesting Yuezhuornis lived on the ground and was likely unable to fly. Rather than a straight march toward flight, early bird evolution already included branches heading in the opposite direction.
why_it_matters: It shows bird evolution was not a straight march toward flight, but included branches trying different ways of life, which changes how scientists read the history of life on Earth.

background_read: Birds are living things descended from small meat-eating dinosaurs, so early birds often show a mix of bird and dinosaur features.
A fossil is the preserved remains of an ancient living thing, and it can show how bodies changed over time.
Scientists place a fossil on the family tree by comparing its bones with those of other living things.
Flight is not the only way of life for birds: some modern birds live mostly on the ground, and their leg shapes suit walking rather than flying.
